title: Programme Fit and Machine Placement on the Vending Services Program
content:
A Vending Services Program agreement is drawn up against the programme whose entry gate the site meets on headcount, expected monthly sales, dedicated power and loading access, and the machines go into service once they are sited and filled. Where the site does not meet the entry gate of the programme asked for, the agreement is written at the highest programme whose entry gate the site does meet.

An agreement is only opened or commenced while it stands proposed or already active, and a proposal withdrawn before signature closes without charge. The standing of the agreement is read from the vending agreement record before either is done, and it is that record rather than the client's description of where matters have reached that settles the point.

The placement charge printed against the programme is raised for each machine when the machines go into service, and the monthly machine lease printed against the same programme is raised from that period onward where the programme carries one.

Machines are placed after the installation lead days printed against the programme, counted in calendar days from signature, and a client asking for an earlier date is offered the earliest the lead time allows.

Vend prices are set from landed product cost at the markup printed against the programme, and price increases are notified the number of days in advance printed against the same programme.

A machine whose sales fall below the minimum printed against the programme for the review months printed against it is reviewed for removal, and is taken out on the removal notice printed against the same programme.

### Points of judgement the rule settles

**Which programme an agreement is written at where the client asks for one its site does not qualify for.** The gate is read on all four counts, and the agreement is written at the highest programme whose gate the site does meet. Where a site meets the gates of several programmes, it is the highest of those that the agreement is written at, rather than the one the client asked for or the lowest of those the site qualifies for.

**Whether an agreement standing suspended or closed admits an opening or a commencement.** It does not. Only an agreement standing proposed, or one already active, admits either.

**What is charged when a proposal never reaches signature.** A proposal withdrawn before signature closes without charge, so no placement charge and no lease arise on it.

**When the lease begins.** The lease is raised from the period in which the machines go into service onward, and only where the programme held carries a lease at all.

### The lead time worked through (hypothetical dates)

On a programme whose installation lead days stand at 15, the lead time is counted in calendar days from signature, so machines are placed after those 15 calendar days have run from the day the agreement was signed. A client signing on the first of a month and asking for placement on the tenth is offered the earliest date the lead time allows rather than the date asked for. The lead figure used here is an illustration of the counting and is not itself a rule about any one programme.
